title: Hosea Chapter 11 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Hosea chapter 11 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Hosea Chapter 11 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Hosea Chapter 11.

questions.question: According to Hosea 11:1, from where did God call His son, Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Egypt
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:1 states, 'When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.'

questions.question: In Hosea 11:2, to what did the people sacrifice and burn incense?
questions.correctAnswer: Baalim and graven images
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:2 says, 'they sacrificed unto Baalim, and burned incense to graven images.'

questions.question: Who did God teach to go by taking them by their arms, according to Hosea 11:3?
questions.correctAnswer: Ephraim
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:3 states, 'I taught Ephraim also to go, taking them by their arms.'

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 11:4 says God laid meat unto Israel and drew them with cords of a man.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:4 states, 'I drew them with cords of a man... and I laid meat unto them.'

questions.question: According to Hosea 11:5, who will be king over Israel because they refused to return to Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: The Assyrian
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:5 says, 'but the Assyrian shall be his king, because they refused to return.'

questions.question: What will abide on Israel's cities and consume their branches, according to Hosea 11:6?
questions.correctAnswer: The sword
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:6 states, 'And the sword shall abide on his cities, and shall consume his branches.'

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 11:7 describes God's people as steadfast and faithful to Him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:7 says, 'my people are bent to backsliding from me,' indicating unfaithfulness.

questions.question: In Hosea 11:8, what does God say about His heart toward Ephraim?
options: His heart is turned within Him and His repentings are kindled together
He is angry and ready to give them up
questions.correctAnswer: His heart is turned within Him and His repentings are kindled together
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:8 states, 'mine heart is turned within me, my repentings are kindled together.'

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 11:9 states that God will destroy Ephraim in His anger.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:9 says, 'I will not execute the fierceness of mine anger... I will not return to destroy Ephraim.'

questions.question: According to Hosea 11:10, what will the LORD do that causes the children to tremble?
questions.correctAnswer: Roar like a lion
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:10 states, 'he shall roar like a lion: when he shall roar, then the children shall tremble.'

questions.question: What birds are mentioned in Hosea 11:11 as trembling out of Egypt and Assyria?
questions.correctAnswer: Bird and dove
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:11 says, 'They shall tremble as a bird out of Egypt, and as a dove out of the land of Assyria.'

questions.question: According to Hosea 11:12, which tribe is said to rule with God and be faithful with the saints?
questions.correctAnswer: Judah
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:12 states, 'but Judah yet ruleth with God, and is faithful with the saints.'

questions.question: In Hosea 11, which event happened first?
options: God called His son out of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: God called His son out of Egypt
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:1 mentions God calling His son out of Egypt before the other events described in later verses.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 11:3 reveals that Ephraim knew God healed them.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:3 says, 'but they knew not that I healed them,' indicating Ephraim did not know.

questions.question: According to Hosea 11:7, when the people called to the Most High, how many exalted Him?
questions.correctAnswer: None at all
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:7 states, 'though they called them to the most High, none at all would exalt him.'

medium.title: Hosea Chapter 11 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Hosea Chapter 11 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Hosea 11:5, why will Israel not return to the land of Egypt?
options: Because God commanded them to stay
Because the Assyrian king forbade it
questions.correctAnswer: Because they refused to return
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:5 states that Israel shall not return into the land of Egypt because they refused to return. This shows their disobedience led to consequences. Verses 5 and 7 together emphasize Israel's refusal and backsliding.

questions.question: What consequence does Hosea 11:6 describe that will come upon Israel's cities?
options: The sword shall abide and consume its branches
They will prosper and be fruitful
The cities will be rebuilt by their enemies
Peace will reign over the land
questions.correctAnswer: The sword shall abide and consume its branches
questions.explanation: Verse 6 warns that the sword will remain on Israel's cities, consuming their branches and devouring them because of their own counsels, indicating judgment due to their disobedience and poor decisions.

questions.question: How does Hosea 11:7 describe the spiritual condition of Israel's people?
options: They are bent to backsliding and do not exalt the Most High
They are faithful and call to God
questions.correctAnswer: They are bent to backsliding and do not exalt the Most High
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:7 explains Israel's people are inclined to backsliding from God and, despite calling to the Most High, none would exalt Him, highlighting their spiritual failure and pride.

questions.question: What internal struggle does God express in Hosea 11:8 regarding Israel?
options: His heart is turned within him and his repentings are kindled together
He is indifferent towards their fate
He is angry and ready to abandon them
He is pleased with their repentance
questions.correctAnswer: His heart is turned within him and his repentings are kindled together
questions.explanation: In verse 8, God wrestles emotionally with how to give up Israel, showing compassion as His heart is turned inward and His repentings (relenting) are kindled, revealing divine mercy despite their sin.

questions.question: According to Hosea 11:9, why does God choose not to destroy Ephraim fully?
options: Because He is God and not man, and the Holy One in their midst
Because they promised to obey Him
Because another nation interceded for them
questions.correctAnswer: Because He is God and not man, and the Holy One in their midst
questions.explanation: Verse 9 explains God will not execute the fierceness of anger or destroy Ephraim because of His divine nature, emphasizing mercy and holiness present among His people.

questions.question: What does Hosea 11:10 say will happen to the children of Israel when the LORD roars like a lion?
options: The children shall tremble from the west
questions.correctAnswer: The children shall tremble from the west
questions.explanation: Verse 10 describes God's powerful roar like a lion causing the children of Israel to tremble from the west, symbolizing fear and recognition of God's authority and judgement.

questions.question: How does Hosea 11:11 describe the return of Israel to their homes?
options: They shall tremble as a bird out of Egypt and as a dove out of Assyria
They shall be led by a prophet
They shall rebuild their cities with joy
questions.correctAnswer: They shall tremble as a bird out of Egypt and as a dove out of Assyria
questions.explanation: Verse 11 uses similes of trembling birds and doves to describe Israel's fearful but guided return home, indicating God's protective care despite their prior disobedience.

questions.question: What accusation does God make against Ephraim in Hosea 11:12?
options: Ephraim compasses God about with lies and the house of Israel with deceit
Ephraim is faithful and obeys God
questions.correctAnswer: Ephraim compasses God about with lies and the house of Israel with deceit
questions.explanation: Verse 12 accuses Ephraim and Israel of deceit and lies against God, contrasting with Judah's faithfulness, illustrating spiritual failure and hypocrisy.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 11:6 teaches that the sword will consume Israel’s branches because of their own counsels.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:6 clearly states that the sword will remain on Israel’s cities and consume their branches because of their own counsels, showing that their plans led to destruction.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 11:7 says that although Israel called to the Most High, many exalted Him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 7 states that although Israel called to the Most High, none at all would exalt Him, highlighting their failure to honor God truly.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 11:9 shows God's mercy by declaring He will not enter into the city to destroy Ephraim.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:9 expresses God's mercy and holiness by indicating He will not execute fierce anger or enter the city to destroy Ephraim, despite their sins.

questions.question: What does Hosea 11:5 imply will happen if Israel refuses to return to God?
options: They will return to Egypt safely
God will protect them from enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Assyria will become their king
questions.explanation: Verse 5 states that because Israel refused to return, the Assyrian will be their king, indicating foreign domination as a consequence of disobedience.

questions.question: Based on Hosea 11:8 and 11:9, what biblical virtue is demonstrated by God in His dealings with Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy and compassion
questions.explanation: Verses 8 and 9 show God's internal struggle and His choice to withhold full judgment, demonstrating His mercy and compassion towards Israel despite their sin.

questions.question: How does Hosea 11:6-7 together teach about the consequences of unfaithfulness to God?
options: Unfaithfulness leads to destruction and spiritual backsliding
questions.correctAnswer: Unfaithfulness leads to destruction and spiritual backsliding
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 7 together show that Israel's own misguided counsel brings sword and destruction, while their people are spiritually backsliding and not exalting God, illustrating consequences of unfaithfulness.

questions.question: A believer struggles with feelings of abandonment due to their failures. Based on Hosea 11:8-9, what biblical truth can encourage them?
options: God’s heart is turned inward with compassion, and He chooses mercy over destruction
They must earn God’s favor by works
questions.correctAnswer: God’s heart is turned inward with compassion, and He chooses mercy over destruction
questions.explanation: Verses 8-9 reveal God’s internal anguish and decision not to destroy Israel, showing His compassionate mercy even when people fail, offering hope for those struggling with failure.

hard.title: Hosea Chapter 11 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Hosea Chapter 11.

questions.question: In Hosea 11:9, what reason does God give for not destroying Ephraim despite His anger?
options: Because He is merciful and forgives all sins
Because He is God, not man, and the Holy One in their midst
Because Ephraim was chosen to be His servant
questions.correctAnswer: Because He is God, not man, and the Holy One in their midst
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:9 states that God will not destroy Ephraim because He is God and not man, emphasizing His divine nature and presence among them, which restrains His anger.

questions.question: What metaphor is used in Hosea 11:10 to describe the LORD's coming, and what is its effect on the children?
options: The LORD is like a gentle shepherd, comforting the children
The LORD shall roar like a lion, causing the children to tremble
The LORD is like a storm, shaking the mountains
The LORD is like a whisper, guiding the children softly
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD shall roar like a lion, causing the children to tremble
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:10 uses the metaphor of the LORD roaring like a lion, symbolizing His powerful judgment, which causes the children to tremble from the west.

questions.question: According to Hosea 11:11, from which lands will Ephraim and the children tremble and be placed in their houses?
questions.correctAnswer: Egypt and Assyria
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:11 says the children shall tremble as a bird out of Egypt and as a dove out of the land of Assyria, and they will be placed in their houses by the LORD.

questions.question: What accusation does God make against Ephraim and the house of Israel in Hosea 11:12?
options: They are faithful and rule with God
They have turned to idolatry and false gods
They compass God about with lies and deceit
They have repented and returned to God
questions.correctAnswer: They compass God about with lies and deceit
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:12 accuses Ephraim and the house of Israel of surrounding God with lies and deceit, highlighting their unfaithfulness.

questions.question: Which tribe is described in Hosea 11:12 as ruling with God and being faithful with the saints?
questions.correctAnswer: Judah
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:12 contrasts Ephraim’s deceit with Judah’s faithfulness, stating that Judah rules with God and is faithful with the saints.

questions.question: How does Hosea 11:8 express God’s internal conflict regarding Israel, and which ancient cities are referenced as a comparison for destruction?
options: God is joyful and references Jerusalem and Bethlehem
God is indifferent and references Nineveh and Babylon
God’s heart is turned within Him, referencing Admah and Zeboim
God is angry and references Sodom and Gomorrah
questions.correctAnswer: God’s heart is turned within Him, referencing Admah and Zeboim
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:8 shows God's internal struggle about giving up Israel, comparing it to destroying Admah and Zeboim, cities destroyed alongside Sodom and Gomorrah.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 11:9 reveals that God’s decision not to destroy Ephraim is because He is like man in His judgment.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:9 states the opposite—that God will not destroy Ephraim because He is God and not man, emphasizing His divine mercy rather than human impulsiveness.

questions.question: True or False: The imagery in Hosea 11:10 of the LORD roaring like a lion is an example of a literary device called a simile.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:10 uses 'like a lion' to compare the LORD's roar, an explicit simile that conveys power and fear.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God calling His son out of Egypt, as referenced in Hosea 11:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 2:15
questions.explanation: Matthew 2:15 quotes Hosea 11:1 when describing Joseph bringing Jesus out of Egypt, fulfilling the prophetic typology of God calling His son out of Egypt.

questions.question: How does the Hebrew word translated as "compasseth" in Hosea 11:12 contribute to the understanding of Israel's deceit towards God?
options: It means to protect or shield
It means to surround or encompass
It means to help or support
It means to praise or worship
questions.correctAnswer: It means to surround or encompass
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'compasseth' (סָבַב, savav) means to surround or encompass, implying that Israel surrounds God with lies, highlighting their pervasive deceit (Hosea 11:12).

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'I drew them with cords of a man, with bands of love' in Hosea 11:4 in terms of ancient Near Eastern covenant imagery?
options: It refers to military conquest and forced submission
It symbolizes a gentle, loving guidance and covenant bond
It implies economic transaction and trade agreements
It depicts punishment through physical restraint
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes a gentle, loving guidance and covenant bond
questions.explanation: In Hosea 11:4, the imagery of cords and bands signifies tender, loving care and covenantal relationship, common in ancient Near Eastern contexts for shepherds and family bonds.

questions.question: According to Hosea 11:5, who will be king over Israel because they refused to return to Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: The Assyrian
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:5 states the Assyrian shall be king over Israel because they refused to return to Egypt, indicating foreign domination as judgment.

questions.question: How does Hosea 11:7 describe the spiritual condition of God’s people in relation to backsliding and worship?
options: They are fully faithful and exalt the Most High
They are bent to backsliding and do not exalt the Most High
They are indifferent but call on the Most High
They worship idols but secretly honor God
questions.correctAnswer: They are bent to backsliding and do not exalt the Most High
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:7 declares God's people are inclined to backsliding and though they call to the Most High, none exalt Him, showing their spiritual unfaithfulness.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage quotes Hosea 11:1 to illustrate Jesus' early life and divine calling?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 2:15
questions.explanation: Matthew 2:15 quotes Hosea 11:1 when Joseph brings Jesus out of Egypt, showing Jesus as the fulfillment of the prophetic 'son called out of Egypt' typology.

questions.question: What does Hosea 11:6 predict will happen to Israel’s cities and branches, and why?
options: They will flourish because of their faithfulness
They will be destroyed because of their own counsels
They will be protected by God from enemies
They will be taken captive by Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: They will be destroyed because of their own counsels
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:6 foretells that the sword will remain on Israel’s cities, consuming their branches due to their own counsels, emphasizing self-destructive choices.

theological.title: Hosea Chapter 11 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Hosea Chapter 11 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Hosea 11:1 reveal about God's relationship with Israel in their early history?
options: God loved Israel as a child and called His son out of Egypt
Israel was independent and rejected God's call
God punished Israel for their disobedience from the start
questions.correctAnswer: God loved Israel as a child and called His son out of Egypt
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:1 states that when Israel was a child, God loved him and called His son out of Egypt, indicating a tender, parental love from the beginning. This foreshadows God's covenantal relationship with Israel and Christ's typological role (Exodus 4:22-23).

questions.question: According to Hosea 11:2, what was Israel's response to God's calling?
options: They sacrificed to Baalim and burned incense to graven images
They remained faithful to God alone
questions.correctAnswer: They sacrificed to Baalim and burned incense to graven images
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:2 explains that despite God's calling, Israel went after other gods, sacrificing to Baalim and burning incense to graven images, demonstrating their idolatry and unfaithfulness.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily demonstrated in Hosea 11:3 when God says, 'I taught Ephraim also to go, taking them by their arms'?
questions.correctAnswer: God's nurturing guidance
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:3 reveals God's nurturing guidance as He tenderly leads Ephraim like a child learning to walk, showing God's patient care in sanctification (Psalm 23:3).

questions.question: How does Hosea 11:4 portray God's love for Israel?
options: God drew them with cords of a man and bands of love
God abandoned them to their own devices
God demanded perfect obedience with strict laws
questions.correctAnswer: God drew them with cords of a man and bands of love
questions.explanation: According to Hosea 11:4, God’s love is tender and relational, likened to drawing Israel with cords and bands of love, showing His merciful and covenantal care (Jeremiah 31:3).

questions.question: What theological teaching concerning divine judgment and human rebellion is found in Hosea 11:5?
options: The Assyrian shall be their king because they refused to return
God will restore Israel to Egypt
Israel will be free from foreign oppression
The land of Egypt will become a place of refuge
questions.correctAnswer: The Assyrian shall be their king because they refused to return
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:5 teaches that due to Israel's refusal to repent, God will allow the Assyrian to rule over them, affirming the doctrine of divine judgment for persistent rebellion (Isaiah 10:5).

questions.question: What does Hosea 11:6 predict about the consequences of Israel's counsels?
options: The sword shall abide on their cities and consume their branches
Their cities will prosper and be secure
They will be given peace and rest
questions.correctAnswer: The sword shall abide on their cities and consume their branches
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:6 indicates that because of their own counsels, Israel will face violent consequences symbolized by the sword consuming their cities, highlighting the doctrine of retributive justice.

questions.question: In Hosea 11:7, what is Israel's spiritual condition despite calling to the Most High?
options: They are bent to backsliding and none exalt Him
They are wholly faithful and obedient
questions.correctAnswer: They are bent to backsliding and none exalt Him
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:7 describes Israel as backsliding and failing to truly exalt God, revealing their covenant unfaithfulness and spiritual apostasy.

questions.question: What divine emotion is expressed by God in Hosea 11:8 when He contemplates giving up Israel?
options: God’s heart is turned within, and repentings are kindled together
questions.correctAnswer: God’s heart is turned within, and repentings are kindled together
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:8 reveals God's deep internal conflict and compassion, showing His merciful nature as His heart is moved and repentings are kindled, indicating the attribute of divine mercy and sorrow over judgment (Psalm 78:38).

questions.question: Which attribute of God does Hosea 11:9 emphasize in His decision not to destroy Ephraim?
options: God's holiness and mercy as the Holy One, not man
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness and mercy as the Holy One, not man
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:9 highlights God’s unique divine nature—His holiness and mercy—and that unlike man, He will not destroy Ephraim, underscoring God’s graciousness and sovereign restraint (Exodus 34:6-7).

questions.question: How does Hosea 11:10 depict the LORD’s future leadership over His people?
options: He shall roar like a lion and the children shall tremble
He will be silent and allow them to lead themselves
He will abandon them to their enemies
He will quietly lead them without power
questions.correctAnswer: He shall roar like a lion and the children shall tremble
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:10 portrays God as a powerful lion whose roar causes trembling, symbolizing His sovereign and awe-inspiring leadership in the eschatological restoration of His people (Amos 3:8).

questions.question: What combined teaching about restoration and judgment is conveyed by Hosea 11:5-6 and Hosea 11:11?
options: Israel will face judgment under Assyria but will ultimately be placed back in their homes by the LORD
Israel will be permanently destroyed and never restored
Egypt will become Israel's refuge and protector
The LORD will abandon Israel to foreign powers forever
questions.correctAnswer: Israel will face judgment under Assyria but will ultimately be placed back in their homes by the LORD
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:5-6 predicts judgment through Assyrian rule and sword, while 11:11 promises eventual restoration and placement in their homes, teaching the doctrine of divine chastening followed by restoration (Jeremiah 30:3).

questions.question: What does Hosea 11:12 teach about the differing spiritual conditions of Israel and Judah?
options: Israel surrounds God with lies and deceit, but Judah rules with God and is faithful
Both Israel and Judah are equally faithful
Judah is more deceitful than Israel
Israel and Judah both reject God
questions.correctAnswer: Israel surrounds God with lies and deceit, but Judah rules with God and is faithful
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:12 contrasts Israel's deceitful rebellion with Judah's relative faithfulness and rule with God, illustrating the doctrine of covenant faithfulness varying among God's people (2 Chronicles 19:8).

questions.question: How does Hosea 11:1-4 collectively illustrate the doctrine of sanctification in God's covenant people?
options: God nurtures and teaches Israel with loving care, guiding them despite their ignorance
Israel sanctifies themselves by their own strength
God demands immediate perfection without guidance
questions.correctAnswer: God nurtures and teaches Israel with loving care, guiding them despite their ignorance
questions.explanation: Verses 1-4 show God’s patient and loving nurture—calling Israel, teaching Ephraim to walk, drawing them with cords of love—highlighting sanctification as God’s work in His covenant people (Philippians 1:6).

questions.question: What apologetic response does Hosea 11:8-9 provide to the sceptic’s claim that God is unjust for not punishing Israel fully?
options: God’s heart is moved with compassion and He chooses mercy over destruction, showing His justice balanced with mercy
God punishes without mercy or reason
God’s actions are arbitrary and unpredictable
questions.correctAnswer: God’s heart is moved with compassion and He chooses mercy over destruction, showing His justice balanced with mercy
questions.explanation: Hosea 11:8-9 shows God wrestling with judgment but withholding destruction out of mercy, affirming His just and merciful nature which answers sceptical claims of injustice (Exodus 34:6-7).

questions.question: How does Hosea 11:10-11 use animal imagery to depict God's restoration of Israel in the redemptive narrative?
options: God's roar causes trembling and He brings them out like birds from Egypt and Assyria
God abandons Israel like lost sheep
God uses harsh beasts to punish Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God's roar causes trembling and He brings them out like birds from Egypt and Assyria
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 use the lion’s roar and the imagery of birds leaving captivity to portray God’s powerful restoration of Israel, fitting the biblical theme of deliverance from exile (Psalm 91:13).
